doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: Where his compositions come from and keeping anger out
summary: He writes from a specific subject, a feeling or a motif, and tries to keep anger out of his music.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. So when you write a composition, is there usually something specific that gets your attention and that you feel the need to work on something new and express your reaction to it? Or is it more of a general sense of America and the world?

Well it’s – the music may come from different things. It may be about something specific, it may be about just a feeling or it might be about a certain motif that came into my head, a certain little melody and then I might develop that. It just depends on the frame of mind, which is different from day to day. I don’t have one way of doing things.
Do you write different when you’re angry than when you’re not?
I try to keep anger out of it. I think that, so it’s difficult to answer that because I can’t see myself doing music while angry. I don’t see myself as being productive in any way by
being angry so anger is something when I feel it then I observe myself and decide that I’m not going to be angry because it doesn’t help anything.
